title: Probe, attribute, and untangle a model
brief: Train a probe against a control, share an output among features with integrated gradients and exact Shapley values, and recover planted features with a sparse autoencoder.
hints: On the worked model f(x) = x0*x1 + 2*x2 at x = [2, 3, 1], the gradient is [3, 2, 2], so gradient times input is [6, 6, 2]. Integrated gradients and Shapley values both give [3, 3, 2]. The three values sum to 8 = f(x) - f(0).

Midpoint integrated gradients: with steps = 4 the points on the path are at a = 0.125, 0.375, 0.625, 0.875. Average the gradient there, then multiply by (x - baseline). Forgetting that last factor is the most common mistake.
Shapley weights for n = 3 features: a subset of size 0 or 2 has weight 1/3, a subset of size 1 has weight 1/6. They sum to one over the four subsets that exclude feature i: 1/3 + 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/3.
The probe gradient is H.T @ (sigmoid(z) - y) / n + l2 * w with z = H @ w + b. For a loss that never overflows, use np.logaddexp(0, z) - y * z.

In the sparse autoencoder, the gate (pre > 0) appears twice: once to mask the gradient that flows into the encoder, and once inside the L1 term, where the slope of relu(pre) is 1 on active units and 0 elsewhere.
